references.text: Moses receives the command again to make everything according to the pattern (תַּבְנִית) he was shown on the mountain, repeating the same principle from verse 9.
Moses is to set up the tabernacle according to the pattern he was shown on the mountain, a direct parallel to the instruction in Exodus 25:9.
The altar is to be made as Moses was shown on the mountain, following the same principle of adhering to the divine pattern.
The lampstand was made according to the pattern the Lord had shown Moses, fulfilling the instruction in Exodus 25:9.
David gives Solomon the pattern (תַּבְנִית) for the temple, which he received by the Spirit, paralleling how Moses received the pattern for the tabernacle.
David explains that the entire plan for the temple came from the hand of the Lord, just as Moses received the tabernacle's pattern from God.
Stephen refers to the fact that the tabernacle was made according to the pattern (τύπος) that Moses saw, a direct reference to Exodus 25:9.
The book of Hebrews quotes that Moses was warned to make everything according to the pattern he was shown on the mountain, explaining that the tabernacle was a shadow of heavenly things.
The earthly tabernacle is described as a copy of the heavenly one, further clarifying the meaning of the pattern Moses was shown.
A strong thematic parallel confirming that God's house must always be built and maintained according to the exact divine blueprint (the pattern).
